claim: the drop -> collect -> buff -> compose path runs end to end in a live simulation, and the drop's slabId resolves against the composed floor
method: createDefenseRun({stageId:'cinder-span',seed:71}) driven through queueInput MOVE/BASIC_ATTACK and advanceDefenseRun, accumulating run.events every tick and deduping by eventId. Read in a real browser module context so the shipped ES modules resolve exactly as the game loads them.
whyThisWasNeeded: Unit tests cannot reach this path. rollBuffDrop fires from resolveDeaths, so a drop requires a real enemy death, then collection inside pickupRange, then buff composition. A short trash-only run is also not evidence: BASIC chance is 600bp, so P(zero drops at 20 kills) is about 29% -- an underpowered sample looks identical to a broken feature.

whatEachFactProves.slabId cinder-span:slab-03: the frozen 12-slab table and the composed floor GLB agree -- the drop landed on a real authored slab, not a null lookup
whatEachFactProves.magnitude 1200: integer basis points, so no float entered serialized state
whatEachFactProves.snapshotBuffs 1 and buffStats present: the conditional snapshot fields appear only while a buff is active, which is what keeps a zero-buff run byte-identical to pre-cycle-10

notProvenHere: the drop MODEL rendering in WebGL -- the buff drops resolve to prop-sprite-sheet-single-object.03/.05, both already in all three asset allowlists, so no new mesh ships and no 404 is possible, but the visual instantiation is not asserted by this run
the seven determinism gate checks from item-drop-timed-buff-spec.md section 9 -- authored separately
correctedMisreading: An earlier probe reported 22898 ENEMY_DEFEATED over 553 ticks and zero drops, which looked like a defect. It was double counting: the loop re-read run.events without deduping by eventId, and the run stalls at tick 553 without player input. The real figure was 4 deaths, whose expected drop count is 0.24.
